user.title: Jablotron Futura
user.description: Enter the address of your Futura unit. Modbus TCP must be enabled on the unit, and it accepts only one client at a time.

data_description.name: Also the start of every entity ID, so each unit needs its own.
data_description.unit_id: Leave this at 1. The Futura answers only unit ID 1, and addressing another ID makes it drop the connection.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the unit. Check the address, and that nothing else is holding its single Modbus connection.
error.invalid_response: The unit answered but rejected the request.
error.name_taken: Another unit already uses this name, and its entity IDs would collide. Choose a different one.
error.not_a_futura: That device is not a Jablotron Futura.

abort.already_configured: This Futura is already set up.

data_description.scan_interval: How often live readings are refreshed. The unit has a single socket, so avoid going below 10 seconds.
data_description.slow_interval: How often configuration and statistics are refreshed.
data_description.enable_corrections: Adds the per-sensor temperature offset registers. Each costs an extra Modbus request.
data_description.enable_external_sensors: Lets Home Assistant push its own temperature, humidity and CO2 readings into the Futura.
data_description.enable_external_buttons: Exposes the external boost button registers.

set_away.name: Set away period
set_away.description: Sets the holiday period. Times are stored on the unit as local wall-clock time.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Which Futura to target. Needed only when more than one is configured.

end.name: Ends
end.description: Defaults to seven days after the start.

duration.description: Seconds to run for; 0 stops the function. Night and party accept up to 36000 (10 h), the rest up to 7200 (2 h).

set_external_sensor.name: Feed an external sensor
set_external_sensor.description: Pushes a Home Assistant reading into one of the Futura's eight external sensor slots so its automatic mode can use it.
